title: Feeling ill: Mir tut der Kopf weh (Gesundheit)
summary: Name the parts of the body, say what hurts and how you feel, and get through the doctor's and the pharmacy.
goals: Say what hurts: Mir tut der Kopf weh. Ich habe Kopfschmerzen.
Say how you feel: Ich bin krank. Ich habe Fieber.
Make an appointment and understand simple instructions at the doctor's

nicosWeg.title: Nicos Weg A1, chapter 17: Health (Geht es dir gut?, Beim Arzt, Gute Besserung!, Nehmen Sie ...)

points: Feeling unwell: [[Ich bin krank.]], [[Ich fühle mich nicht wohl.]], [[Mir geht es nicht gut.]] [[Ich bin krank.]] is the safety net that always works.

Pains are compounds with [[Schmerzen]], usually plural: [[Kopfschmerzen]], [[Rückenschmerzen]] (back), [[Zahnschmerzen]], [[Bauchschmerzen]] (stomach), [[Ohrenschmerzen]], [[Halsschmerzen]] (sore throat).
Or with [[wehtun]], a separable dative verb: [[Mein Kopf tut weh.]], [[Mir tut der Kopf weh.]] Plural: [[Mir tun die Ohren weh.]]

Illnesses with [[haben]]: [[Ich habe Fieber.]], [[Ich habe eine Grippe.]] (flu), [[Ich habe eine Erkältung.]] (a cold), [[Ich habe Schnupfen.]] (a runny nose), [[Ich habe Husten.]] (a cough), [[Ich habe Durchfall.]] (diarrhoea).

Injuries (reflexive, A2; learn them as chunks): [[Ich habe mich am Bein verletzt.]] ([[am]] for der and das words, [[an der]] for die words), [[Ich habe mir den Arm gebrochen.]] And [[Mir ist schlecht.]] (I feel sick)
Advice uses the imperative, and [[viel]] fits almost anything: [[Trink viel Tee und geh schlafen.]] End with [[Gute Besserung!]] (get well soon), which you can say to anyone.

phrases.en: I have a headache and a temperature.

phrases.de: Ich habe mich an der Hand verletzt.
Ich habe mir das Bein gebrochen.
Trink viel Tee und geh schlafen.
phrases.en: Drink lots of tea and go to bed.

notes.extra: Injuries ([[Ich habe mich verletzt.]], [[Ich habe mir den Arm gebrochen.]]) and giving advice with the imperative.

points: [[der Körperteil]], plural [[die Körperteile]]: a part of the body. Learn each with its article and plural.

Head and face: [[der Kopf]], [[das Gesicht]], [[die Haare]], [[die Stirn]] (forehead), [[das Auge]], [[die Augenbraue]], [[die Nase]], [[die Wange]] (cheek), [[der Mund]], [[die Lippe]], [[der Zahn]], [[das Kinn]] (chin), [[das Ohr]], [[der Hals]] (neck, throat), [[der Bart]] (beard).
Arms and hands: [[die Schulter]], [[der Arm]], [[der Ellenbogen]] (elbow), [[das Handgelenk]] (wrist), [[die Hand]], [[der Finger]], [[der Daumen]] (thumb), [[der Nagel]].

Body and legs: [[die Brust]] (chest), [[der Bauch]] (belly), [[der Rücken]] (back), [[die Hüfte]] (hip), [[das Bein]], [[das Knie]], [[die Wade]] (calf), [[der Fuß]], [[das Fußgelenk]] (ankle), [[die Ferse]] (heel), [[der Zeh]] (toe).
Careful with near twins: [[das Kinn]] (chin) and [[das Kind]] (child).
notes.extra: About 40 body parts with plurals, many more than the lesson's table.

points: Words: [[der Arzt]], [[die Ärztin]], [[der Patient]], [[die Patientin]], [[die Arztpraxis]] (doctor's practice), [[die Tablette]], [[die Tropfen]] (drops), [[die Salbe]] (ointment), [[das Rezept]] (prescription; also a recipe).
What the doctor does: [[den Patienten untersuchen]] (examine), [[den Blutdruck messen]] (take blood pressure), [[Medikamente verschreiben]] (prescribe).
Make an appointment first if you can, usually by phone. You'll be asked about your symptoms: [[Was haben Sie für Beschwerden?]] Bring your health insurance card ([[die Versichertenkarte]]).
At the doctor's: [[Wie kann ich Ihnen helfen?]] or [[Was fehlt Ihnen?]], then [[Seit wann haben Sie die Schmerzen?]] - [[Seit gestern.]]
During the examination: [[Wo tut es weh?]], [[Machen Sie bitte den Mund auf.]], [[Husten Sie bitte.]]

The verdict and advice: [[Es ist nichts Schlimmes.]], [[Sie haben eine Grippe.]], [[Ich schreibe Ihnen ein Rezept.]], [[Bleiben Sie im Bett.]] A sick note for work is [[die Arbeitsunfähigkeitsbescheinigung]]. Use [[Sie]] with the doctor.

phrases.de: Bitte bringen Sie Ihre Versichertenkarte mit.

phrases.en: How long have you had the pain?

notes.extra: Phoning for an appointment, the examination ([[Machen Sie bitte den Mund auf.]]) and the words for medicine: [[Tablette]], [[Tropfen]], [[Salbe]], [[Rezept]].

sections.title: What hurts?
sections.text:
Two ways to say it:
- [[Mir tut der Kopf weh.]] = My head hurts. Literally: to me, the head does pain. More than one: [[Mir tun die Füße weh.]]
- [[Ich habe Kopfschmerzen.]] = I have a headache. Also [[Bauchschmerzen]], [[Halsschmerzen]], [[Rückenschmerzen]], [[Zahnschmerzen]].

[[wehtun]] is separable and the person is in the dative (lesson 5): [[Tut dir etwas weh?]] = Does something hurt? [[Wo tut es weh?]] = Where does it hurt?

Russian у меня болит голова has the same shape: the body part is the subject, and the person is not. German puts the person in the dative ([[mir]]), Russian uses у меня. Armenian says գլուխս ցավում է, 'my head hurts', like English.

sections.title: How do you feel?
sections.text:
- [[Wie geht es Ihnen?]] - [[Nicht so gut. Ich bin krank.]]
- [[Ich habe Fieber.]] = I have a temperature.
- [[Ich bin müde.]] (Unit 5)
- [[Mir ist schlecht.]] = I feel sick (I might throw up). Another dative chunk.

To someone who is ill: [[Gute Besserung!]] = Get well soon! And when they're better: [[Bist du wieder gesund?]] = Are you well again?

sections.title: At the doctor's
sections.text:
In Germany you usually go first to a general doctor, [[der Hausarzt]] or [[die Hausärztin]], at a [[Praxis]] (practice). Make an appointment by phone or online: [[Ich möchte einen Termin, bitte. Ich habe Fieber.]] At the reception they ask for your health insurance card: [[Ihre Karte, bitte.]]

What the doctor asks and says:
- [[Was fehlt Ihnen?]] = What's the matter? (a dative chunk)
- [[Seit wann haben Sie Fieber?]] - [[Seit zwei Tagen.]] ([[seit]], lesson 1)
- [[Nehmen Sie die Tabletten dreimal am Tag nach dem Essen.]] = Take the tablets three times a day after meals.
- [[Bleiben Sie zu Hause.]] = Stay at home.

You get the medicine ([[das Medikament]]) at [[die Apotheke]] (the pharmacy). A hospital is [[das Krankenhaus]].

sections.title: Two numbers
sections.text: Emergency (ambulance, fire brigade): 112. A doctor at night or at the weekend, when it's not an emergency: 116 117.
